title: Animal matching: VM2 structured output as primary discriminator + MegaDescriptor (BVRA) as tiebreaker
author: jill (operator-directed 2026-09-14, post dog-enrollment + body-scan discussion)
plan_section: v2 animal pipeline completion: enroll operator animals + third-stage embedding model (MegaDescriptor-L-384) for individual animal re-identification, paralleling how face_recognition runs on people after VM1+VM2
trigger: Operator 2026-09-14 (verbatim, directive 1): 'So here is what I am thinking, we already have a well-established pipeline and I do not want to mess with this. I mean, I do not want to mess with changing YOLO vision model 1 or vision model 2, but just like with people, we are going to do basically a third run through of a model and that will be the facial recognition, then with dogs, we can do a third or I guess a fourth run through of the model on this Bohemian animal thing. So it would basically be another add on to the pipeline on the animal branch. So yeah, create some PRD stories for after we get the detailed description of the animal from the VM2 that we then run it into the Bohemian to see if we can recognize enrolled animals.' Operator 2026-09-14 (verbatim, directive 2): 'well that is why I wanted you to look at what the output of VM two said about this dog since it is the only dog that is being enrolled then you can give the option for basically everything with the VM two output has given for the color and type of dog and that will be the match and then we will go to the Bohemian thing to get even better matching.' Operator 2026-09-14 (verbatim, directive 3): 'yes, he is a goldendoodle.' Operator 2026-09-14 (verbatim, directive 4): 'I always want the tier 2 matcher to be run for animals not just on ambiguity' - clarifies that MegaDescriptor (BVRA) cosine runs on EVERY animal alert, not gated by Tier-1 ambiguity. Tier 1 (VM2 feature scoring) is an advisory ranking among Tier-2-acceptable candidates. Three concrete gaps in v2: (1) Pipeline Stage 12 only matches vehicles + persons - animal mode falls through with no match and no TG3. (2) No animal matching infra exists. (3) Animal alerts today carry no per-animal metadata beyond YOLO class + animal/dog/0.X.
background: v2 currently has no animal matching at all. v1 (farm-surveillance-refactor) had a feature-weighted ensemble matcher (animal_matcher.py + animal_schema.py) that scored candidates on distinctive_features + coat_primary_color + body_size + body_build + face_details + coat_pattern + estimated_age + sex_signal. The operator chose a NEW approach: TIER 2 (MegaDescriptor embedding cosine) is the PRIMARY match signal and ALWAYS runs on every animal alert (operator directive 4). TIER 1 (VM2 structured output scoring) is an ADVISORY ranking that breaks ties among Tier-2-acceptable candidates and provides structured metadata for TG#3 rendering. MegaDescriptor: BVRA MegaDescriptor-L-384 from https://huggingface.co/BVRA/MegaDescriptor-L-384, loaded via timm.create_model(hf-hub:BVRA/MegaDescriptor-L-384, pretrained=True), produces 768-dim embedding from 384x384 RGB. Trained on 49 species incl. dogs with ArcFace loss. Weights downloaded at runtime by timm into ~/Library/Caches/huggingface/hub/ - OUTSIDE the repo (no strip needed). Empirical evidence (operator's dog 'Finnegan', replayed through VM2 across 15 alerts today, 2026-09-14): species=dog (15/15), size=medium (15/15), color_pattern={brown: 6, tan: 9} (mixed - set match), breed=null (enum too restrictive), distinctive_features={black collar: 6, curly fur: 3, blue collar: 2, curled tail: 2, curly coat: 1, curly tail: 1}. For Tier-1 ranking: Finnegan's signature = {species: dog, size: medium, color_patterns: {brown, tan}, distinctive_features: {black collar, curly fur, curly coat, curled tail}}. Operator has confirmed: do NOT touch VM1 (YOLO) or VM2 (Qwen-VL).

design_principles: Tier 2 (MegaDescriptor cosine) ALWAYS runs on every animal alert (operator directive 2026-09-14: 'I always want the tier 2 matcher to be run for animals not just on ambiguity'). Tier 2 is the PRIMARY match signal. Tier 1 (VM2 feature scoring) is an ADVISORY ranking - it sorts the cosine candidates by feature compatibility and breaks ties when multiple animals are within cosine threshold.

Match flow: (1) Stage 11b picks the chosen crop via better_crop. (2) MegaDescriptor embeds it -> observed_embedding. (3) Compute cosine similarity between observed_embedding and every enrolled animal's avg embedding. (4) Filter to candidates with cosine >= TIER2_THRESHOLD (default 0.85, tuned by US-045f). (5) Among those, Tier 1 feature score RANKS them (species_eq + size_eq + color_jaccard + distinctive_features_jaccard). (6) Highest combined rank wins. (7) If NO candidate has cosine >= 0.85, return unmatched.

Tier 1 weights: w1=1.0 species_eq + w2=1.0 size_eq + w3=1.5 color_set_jaccard + w4=1.5 distinctive_features_jaccard (lowercase, trim, /; normalize). Tier 1 score range: 0.0 (no features in common) to 4.0 (perfect match). Tier 1 is used as a tiebreaker among Tier-2-acceptable candidates, not as a gate.

MegaDescriptor loads ONCE at module import (infra.animal_embedder.py keeps the model in module-level singleton). Per-alert cost: ~50-200ms embedding + ~5ms cosine vs all enrolled (numpy matrix multiply). Acceptable for current alert rate (~30 animal alerts/day).

Mirror face_recognition pattern: VM1 (YOLO) detects bbox -> VM2 (Qwen-VL) returns structured description + better_crop -> ANIMAL_EMBEDDER (always, Tier 2) -> cosine sim vs enrolled -> Tier 1 feature ranking among matches -> result.

Better crop selection: pipeline Stage 11b (NEW) reads vm2_result.better_crop, picks crop_a or crop_b accordingly. Falls back to crop_a when better_crop is absent or neither. US-044b builds the pick_alert_image_path() helper that US-045 reuses.

Embedding storage: numpy .npz file with named keys = animal ids, values = stacked 768-dim float32 arrays. Index file = known_animals.json with id + label + species + breed + color_patterns (set) + distinctive_features (set) + first_enrolled_iso + sample_image_paths. Tier 1 signature is stored in known_animals.json for ranking.
Cosine similarity: standard (A @ B) / (norm_A * norm_B). Threshold initial = 0.85, tuned in US-045f against Finnegan replay.

animal_matcher.match_animal() returns: matched=True -> {candidate: {id, label, species, breed, color}, cosine_score: float, tier1_score: float, combined_rank: float, runner_ups: [{id, cosine_score, tier1_score}, ...]}; matched=False -> {top_candidates: [{id, label, cosine_score, tier1_score}], threshold: float}.
Test with synthetic embeddings first (numpy random) before plugging MegaDescriptor - keeps unit tests fast + CPU-only.
Single commit per story on main with US-045 in the message.

stories.title: Add animal_matcher/match.py: ALWAYS run MegaDescriptor cosine + Tier-1 feature ranking among cosine-acceptable candidates
stories.scope: animal_matcher/__init__.py exports match_animal(). animal_matcher/match.py implements Tier-2-primary matcher (operator directive 4, 2026-09-14: 'I always want the tier 2 matcher to be run for animals not just on ambiguity'). Flow: (1) pick_alert_image_path() from US-044b returns chosen crop path. (2) observed_embedding = infra.animal_embedder.embed_image(chosen_crop) -> np.ndarray (768,) float32. (3) For each enrolled animal: cosine_sim = (observed @ avg) / (norm_obs * norm_avg). Threshold filter: keep only candidates with cosine >= TIER2_THRESHOLD (default 0.85, env var ANIMAL_MATCH_THRESHOLD overridable). (4) Among cosine-acceptable candidates, compute Tier-1 feature score: w1=1.0*species_eq + w2=1.0*size_eq + w3=1.5*color_set_jaccard(vm2.color_pattern vs enrolled.color_patterns) + w4=1.5*distinctive_features_jaccard(lowercase, trim, /; normalize). (5) Sort by Tier-1 score desc; highest wins. Return shape: matched=True -> {candidate: {id, label, species, breed, color}, cosine_score: float, tier1_score: float, combined_rank: float, runner_ups: [{id, cosine_score, tier1_score}]}; matched=False -> {top_candidates: [{id, label, cosine_score, tier1_score}], threshold: 0.85}. Empty enrolled: matched=False immediately (no Tier-2 work needed). animal_matcher/match_animal.py is the function module US-044c imports. Stage 11b calls pick_alert_image_path() and stores chosen path in pipeline result; US-045d reads it. Also produce docs/animal-matching-design.md with the tier-2-primary flow diagram + worked example for Finnegan (Tier 2 cosine 0.9X, Tier 1 score 3.125, combined rank = cosine*0.6 + tier1_norm*0.4 OR a similar weighting decided by the worker; documented in the design doc). stories.notes: Combined-rank weighting: cosine_score (range [-1, 1], typically [0.5, 0.95]) and tier1_score (range [0.0, 4.0]) are on different scales. Worker picks a normalized combination in the design doc; recommended approach: rank_score = tier1_score + 5.0 * cosine_score (cosine on [0,1] scaled to ~[0,5] range so it carries meaningful weight, plus tier1 on [0,4]). Simpler alternative: pure tier-1-rank among cosine-acceptable candidates (no weighted combination, just sort by tier1 desc). Worker decides and documents. Tier 2 (cosine) ALWAYS runs per operator directive 4 - no early-out based on Tier 1. Lazy-load MegaDescriptor inside match_animal() (not at module import) so unit tests can run without the model. Storage load: opens data/known/animals/embeddings.npz + known_animals.json via animal_matcher/storage.py (US-045c). Unit tests pass storage dicts directly. Worked example for Finnegan: vm2_result = {species: dog, size: medium, color_pattern: brown, distinctive_features: [black collar]}; enrolled Finnegan avg embedding produces observed_cosine = 0.92 (above 0.85 threshold); enrolled Finnegan feature signature = {species: dog, size: medium, color_patterns: {brown, tan}, distinctive_features: {black collar, curly fur, curly coat, curled tail}}; Tier 1 score = 1.0 (species) + 1.0 (size) + 0.75 (color Jaccard 1/2) + 0.375 (dist-feat Jaccard 1/4) = 3.125. Compute Tier-1 score matrix: each crop's VM2 features scored against (a) Finnegan enrollment signature + (b) a held-out 'other dog' signature (synthetic: different distinctive_features, same species/size/color). Find Tier-1 score distribution that cleanly separates Finnegan from other dog for ranking. Embed all 15 crops via MegaDescriptor-L-384; compute cosine sim vs Finnegan's avg embedding + vs synthetic 'other dog' avg embedding. CRITICAL: Tier-2 cosine is the primary accept gate (operator directive 4, 2026-09-14: 'I always want the tier 2 matcher to be run for animals not just on ambiguity'). Find Tier-2 cosine threshold (initial guess 0.85) that maximizes Finnegan recall while rejecting the synthetic 'other dog'. Tier-1 weights (w1=w2=1.0, w3=w4=1.5) are flexible - tune them too if the synthetic-dog separation improves with different weights. Output: docs/animal-threshold-tuning.md with two recommended thresholds + reasoning + the actual distribution histograms. Update PRD US-045f acceptance criteria + add the recommended values to animal_matcher/config.py.
